items.title: Thursday recap: Jaguars roll past Ravens, and what it means for fantasy
items.dek: Justice Hill led the way with 18.2 PPR points. How it happened, what it means for every fantasy-relevant player, and who to grab off waivers.
body: The Jaguars rolled past the Ravens, 33-10. The Jaguars are now 6-2, and the Ravens slip to 4-5.
The Jaguars struck first in the first quarter on Bhayshul Tuten's 1-yard touchdown run. The offenses traded blows all day: four touchdowns in all, which is exactly what fantasy managers want to see.

Trevor Lawrence never got going: he went 16 of 26 for 242 yards and a touchdown. That added up to 13.6 PPR points against a 17.3 projection. Chris Rodriguez Jr. did a little more than expected: he carried ten times for 19 yards and a touchdown, adding two catches for 13 yards. That's 11.2 PPR points, 5.7 better than our 5.5 projection. It's still a committee, though: he took 34% of the running back carries. It was a quiet day for Bhayshul Tuten, who carried 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown. Just 8.9 PPR points, 4.1 short of our 13.0 projection. Parker Washington was steady: he caught two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. He scored 14.1 PPR points, about what we projected (12.9). With 28% of the team's targets, he is clearly the first read. Jakobi Meyers did his job: he caught four of six targets for 65 yards. That's 10.5 PPR points, right around the 8.4 we expected.

Joe Fagnano never got going: he finished 10 of 18 for 60 yards, with two interceptions. Just -0.3 PPR points, 9.2 short of our 8.9 projection. Derrick Henry never got going: he carried 17 times for 57 yards. That added up to 5.6 PPR points against an 11.2 projection. He took 65% of the running back carries, the lead role but not all of it. Justice Hill broke out: he carried nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown, adding three catches for 7 yards. That's 18.2 PPR points, more than double the 6.4 we projected; a new season high. It was a quiet day for Zay Flowers, who caught three of six targets for 6 yards. Just 5.3 PPR points, 8.0 short of our 13.3 projection. With 38% of the team's targets, he is clearly the first read.
Justice Hill (RB, BAL): 18.2 points against a 6.4 projection; the role is growing.
Zay Flowers (WR, BAL): 5.3 points on a 13.3 projection, only 6 targets.
Justice Hill (RB, BAL, outside BFF's top 50 at RB, so likely on waivers): 18.2 points on 3 targets and 9 carries. The volume is worth chasing.
The Jaguars visit the Titans in week 10; Trevor Lawrence projects for 18.9 points. The Ravens host the Chargers in week 10; Zay Flowers projects for 13.7 points.

items.title: Thursday recap: Packers beat Panthers, and what it means for fantasy
items.dek: Chuba Hubbard put up 24.9 PPR points. How it happened, every fantasy-relevant line, who's rising, who's falling and who to grab off waivers.
body: The Packers beat the Panthers 27-19. The Packers move to 5-3, while the Panthers fall to 3-4.

The Panthers struck first in the first quarter on a 39-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Neither side could pull away; the lead changed hands three times. The score that decided it came with 6:33 left in the 2nd quarter: Josh Jacobs' 1-yard touchdown run.

Jordan Love paid off for his managers: he went 29 of 40 for 281 yards and three touchdowns, with an interception. That's 21.2 PPR points, 4.0 better than our 17.2 projection. Josh Jacobs paid off for his managers: he carried 17 times for 38 yards and a touchdown, adding six catches for 13 yards and a receiving score. That's 23.1 PPR points, 6.9 better than our 16.2 projection. He handled 81% of the running back carries, and that kind of volume travels week to week. Matthew Golden delivered: he caught seven of 13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown. That's 20.9 PPR points, 7.4 better than our 13.5 projection. With 34% of the team's targets, he is clearly the first read. Christian Watson caught seven of nine targets for 106 yards. That's 15.6 PPR points, right around the 15.0 we expected. Tucker Kraft came through: he caught all six of his targets for 53 yards and a touchdown. That's 17.3 PPR points, 6.4 better than our 10.9 projection, easily his top game of the year.

Bryce Young was a letdown: he was 22 of 39 for 200 yards and a touchdown, with an interception. Just 10.0 PPR points, 6.9 short of our 16.9 projection. Chuba Hubbard broke out: he carried 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown, adding seven catches for 38 yards. That's 24.9 PPR points, well above the 15.2 we projected. He handled 96% of the running back carries, and that kind of volume travels week to week. Tetairoa McMillan was a letdown: he caught five of ten targets for 50 yards. Just 10.0 PPR points, 5.1 short of our 15.1 projection. With 29% of the team's targets, he is clearly the first read. Jalen Coker was steady: he caught two of five targets for 35 yards and a touchdown. That's 11.5 PPR points, right around the 13.3 we expected.
